newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firms as banks seek funds for T-bill sales.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firms as banks seek funds for T-bill sales.

text.p: The rouble firmed on Monday against the dollar, as banks bought up roubles ahead of Wednesday's Treasury bill auctions, dealers said.
rouble/dollar Feb 10 midday Feb 10 early Feb 7 close
"The dollar has fallen strongly, because tomorrow banks have to transfer roubles for the auctions," said Alexei Bukleyev, an Alfa-Bank dealer.
The Finance Ministry will offer 4.5 trillion roubles in 196-day GKO discount Treasury bills (series 22071) and seven trillion roubles in 287-day T-bills (series 22072) on Wednesday.
Dealers said dollar selling for tomorrow delivery was most marked.
"Everyone expects that tomorrow there will be few roubles," Bukleyev said.
Inkombank chief dealer Dzhamil Asfari said foreign-owned banks were the biggest sellers.
Wednesday's auction will be especially good for banks as the central bank cut its refinancing rate to 42 percent from 48 percent from Monday, Bukleyev said.
"It means that the dollar will be cheaper and forex operations less profitable," he said. "Government paper yields have not yet fallen to forex market ones."
